statement: Let R = diag(P, C0) be a small matrix input of total size N ∈ S; the block C0 may be absent. Let I be a set of labels at P such that W(C0) − λh is invertible for every h ∈ I. Work over a field E containing the labeled spectral data at P and the entries of C0, with the formal evaluations allowed by Lemma 4.1. Let Z(s1, s2) ∈ MN (E)⟨⟨s1, s2⟩⟩2 18 have constant term R. These are input matrices: their scalar entries act on the input factor and commute with the old coefficient algebra. For h ∈ I, embed πh at the P block, put π̄h = 1 − πh, and form Sh(Z) = πh(W(Z) − λh)πh − πhW(Z)π̄h (︁ π̄h(W(Z) − λh)π̄h )︁−1 π̄hW(Z)πh. Suppose that every Sh(Z) vanishes in degrees less than ℓ, where ℓ ≥ 1. For each word ω of length ℓ, there are scalars ch,ω ∈ E such that [Sh(Z)]ω = ch,ωπh, (ch,ω)h∈I ∈ (TP |I) ⊗ E. The same conclusion holds for homogeneous degree-ℓ coefficients of perturbations in finitely many ordinary commuting parameters.
